messages:
alex_c: Heads-up: after the driver rollout (nvdriver 537.01) to dedicated GPU pools, we're seeing ~18-25% higher per-token latency for short sequences (seq_len <= 64) on SM86 nodes. Tracepoints show we jumped from the bf16-optimized matmul to the generic fp32 fallback for the attention matmul.

sam_dev: Oof. Any nsys/nvprof traces or kernel lists? can you paste a small excerpt?

alex_c: Pasted a reduced nsys call list below (seq_len=64, batch=8):

```
# nsys samples
matmul_bf16_opt_kernel   0.86ms  (expected)
softmax_fused_kernel     0.42ms
kv_cache_lookup          0.05ms
fallback_gemm_fp32       1.95ms  <-- selected on prod after driver update
attention_out_store      0.10ms
```

Note the same model/profile on SM92/SM8x in staging still picks matmul_bf16_opt. Only SM86 picked fallback. KV cache hit rates unchanged (cache hit ~98%).

maria_s: Could be a capability flag mis-read at runtime. If the runtime thinks FP8/BF16 tensor ops are unavailable it will disable the bf16 kernel path. Any output from the gpu probe?

alex_c: Ran the probe on one affected node, output below:

```
$ rdw_gpu_probe --json
{"device":0, "sm":86, "driver":53701, "tensor_cores":true, "bf16_support":true, "fp8_support":false, "compute_capability":"8.6"}
```

That false fp8_support looks suspicious — hardware supports FP8 via drivers/flags but our probe returned false.

perf-ci: CI perf run linked: https://ci.internal.redwood/perf/runs/5472 — shows the regression correlates exactly with the infra driver bump (537.01).

sam_dev: Two hypotheses: (1) the driver exposes FP8 via a new API that our probe didn't call, so the probe reports false and our kernel selector disables optimized kernels; (2) a subtle driver regression changed the reported capability bit ordering.

maria_s: Quick mitigation: add a runtime override toggle (REDWOOD_FORCE_FP8=1) that forces the selector to treat fp8 as available for sm>=86 nodes. That would restore perf while we debug the probe. Any objections to a short-lived flag? :eyes: :+1:

sam_dev: fine by me. I'll prepare a patch that sets kernel path priority so the bf16/FP8 matmul is selected when either (probe.fp8_support==true) OR (sm>=86 && driver>=53700 && ENV_FORCE_FP8==true). Also add a gated roll-out.

alex_c: Before we flip flags in prod, can we add a unit perf test so this doesn't regress again? Something that runs on CI (emulated or on a small SM86 node) asserting kernel choice for seq_len {16,32,64} and compares latency delta < 10% vs baseline.

sam_dev: I'll add tests under tests/perf/kernel_path_tests.py. Proposed quick test run: `pytest tests/perf/kernel_path_tests.py::test_sm86_short_seq_paths --runslow --node sm86-1` (will be gated behind perf label).

infra-bot: Deploy of nvdriver 537.01 to dedicated-prod completed at 1912407200.

perf-ci: Filed perf issue #1428 with attached traces and CI links.

maria_s: Also a note for long-term: our gpu probe should query both driver-reported capability bits and attempt a microkernel smoke test (e.g., try a small bf16 GEMM via cuBLAS/cublasLt) to validate execution path availability. If the smoke test passes, mark BF16/FP8 as available even if driver flag is missing. That would make selection resilient to driver metadata quirks.

alex_c: Agree. For tracking: created issue INF-3164 to implement the smoke-test + env override + perf test. I will attach the nsys snippet and exact node IDs.

sam_dev: Working on the PR for the override + test harness. Will request review from @maria_s and @alex_c.

alex_c: Thanks — once the override is staged we can roll back driver if anything else pops. For now, avoid changing batching heuristics; this seems purely kernel-path selection due to capability detection.

maria_s: FYI, I also saw a tiny KV cache behavior oddity in one trace where the KV unpack path took slightly longer (0.03ms) after the driver update, but that's noise compared to the 1ms extra on the fallback matmul. We'll keep an eye. :mag:

perf-ci: Adding a perf regression alert rule on the model/route so we'll auto-open if tokens-per-second drops >10% after infra changes.

alex_c: Great. If we can get the override in the next few hours we can run a canary on 2 dedicated nodes and confirm latency is back to baseline.

sam_dev: Will post PR link when ready.

maria_s: :thumbsup:
